cards.text: Moses is near the end of his life, and he recites a song to the whole assembly of Israel, from beginning to end. He opens by calling on the heavens and the earth to listen. Friend, when your first line is addressed to the SKY, everybody in the room sits up straight.

cards.question: Moses wants his teaching to land soft, the way something settles on new grass. What does he want his words to be like?

cards.text: Then he says why he's singing: he will proclaim the name of the LORD. And he gives God a name that's SOLID. Doesn't move, doesn't crack, nothing like my edges back in the drawer.

cards.question: Moses calls God the ___, a name that shows up again and again in this song.

cards.text: His work is perfect, and all His ways are just. But then the song turns: His people have acted corruptly toward Him, a perverse and crooked generation.

cards.question: Moses asks if this is how they repay the LORD, and he reminds them who made them. What does he say the LORD is to them?

cards.text: So Moses says: remember the days of old, and ask your father and your elders, and they'll tell you. Friend, nobody has to ask ME twice. I've got YEARS of junk drawer stories ready to go.
Here's what they'd hear. When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance and set the boundaries of the peoples, the LORD had a portion of His own.

cards.question: Out of all the nations, Moses says the LORD's own portion is His people, Jacob.
Moses goes back to where it all started. Where did the LORD first find Jacob?

cards.text: There He surrounded him, instructed him and guarded him as the apple of His eye. Then Moses paints a picture: an eagle stirring up its nest and hovering over its young.

cards.question: In Moses' picture, the LORD is like that eagle. He spread His ___ to catch them.
Moses says the LORD had help from foreign gods when He led His people.

cards.text: And He fed them: milk, curds, the fat of lambs, the choicest wheat, the finest grapes. Plus honey from the LAST place you'd ever look, and I once lost a chocolate chip in my own mustache for three days.

cards.question: Where does the honey come from in Moses' song?

cards.text: Then Jeshurun, which is another name for Israel, grew fat and kicked. Bloated and gorged, like me after one too many test batches, except I don't kick, I just lie there on my gold base and groan.

cards.question: Full and comfortable, Jeshurun ___ the God who made him.

cards.text: Honey from a ROCK, and they went looking for other gods. They provoked God's jealousy with foreign gods and enraged Him with abominations.

cards.question: Moses says Israel sacrificed, but not to God. Who did they sacrifice to?
The gods Israel turned to were old gods their fathers had always feared.
Moses tells them: "You ignored the ___ who brought you forth; you forgot the God who gave you birth."

cards.text: When the LORD saw this, He rejected them, provoked to anger by His own sons and daughters. Then the LORD Himself speaks.

cards.question: The LORD says He will hide His face from His people.

cards.text: He calls them children of unfaithfulness. They made Him jealous with what is not God, with worthless idols, so He turns it right back around on them.

cards.question: Israel made God jealous with what is not God. How does God say He'll make them jealous?

answers.text: By those who are not a people

cards.text: His anger is a fire that burns to the depths of Sheol. He'll heap disasters on them: hunger, plague, wild beasts and vipers.

cards.question: In the song, the sword and the terror spare the infant and the gray-haired man.

cards.text: Then God says He would have said He'd cut them to pieces and blot out their memory from mankind. But there's an if.

cards.question: What held God back from blotting out the memory of His people?

answers.text: Their enemies would take the credit
Moses would beg Him to stop
Israel would turn back to Him

cards.text: Moses says Israel has no understanding, and if only they were wise, they'd see where this is heading. Then he asks: how could one man chase a THOUSAND, or two put ten thousand to flight?

cards.question: One man chasing a thousand. What does Moses say is the only way that could happen?

answers.text: The LORD had given them up
Their army had grown too small
Their weapons had grown too old

cards.question: Moses says even the enemies admit that their rock is not like Israel's Rock.

cards.text: Then the song turns to vines: their vine is from the vine of Sodom and the fields of Gomorrah. Friend, that is NOT a vineyard you put on the label.

cards.question: What are the grapes from that vine like?

cards.text: Then God speaks again: "Have I not stored up these things, sealed up within My vaults?"

cards.question: In the song, who does God say vengeance belongs to?

cards.text: Their foot will slip, and their doom is coming quickly. And then, right there, the song turns toward hope: the LORD will vindicate His people.

cards.question: The LORD will have compassion on His servants. When?

answers.text: When He sees their strength is gone
When they win their next battle
When they bring a bigger offering

cards.text: God asks where their gods are now, the ones that ate the fat of their sacrifices: let them rise up and help! I picture them like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they've STILL got a little charge left.

cards.question: God says there are other gods besides Him, but He is the greatest.
God says: "I bring death and I give life; I wound and I ___"

cards.text: Then God lifts up His hand to heaven and makes a declaration.

cards.question: When God lifts His hand to heaven and declares, what does He swear by?

cards.text: He'll sharpen His flashing sword and repay those who hate Him. And then the song ends with a call to rejoice.

cards.question: At the end of the song, who does Moses call to rejoice with God's people?

cards.text: The heavens rejoice, God's angels worship Him, and He will cleanse His land and His people. That's the whole song, friend, but this story isn't done yet, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "You ignored the ___ who brought you forth; you forgot the God who gave you birth.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 12 quotes "I bring death and I give life; I wound and I ___", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Moses is near the end of his life. That fact comes from outside the cited verses (Deuteronomy 31:14), and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card cites only 32:3, but it also tells part of 32:4: God's solid, unmovable name. The citation is narrower than what the card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question says Moses 'reminds them who made them.' That setup rules out both wrong answers ('neighbor and friend', 'partner and ally') and points straight to 'Creator', so the pick is no longer a reasoned choice.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites only 32:8, but its last clause ('the LORD had a portion of His own') tells 32:9.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer is a kind of place ('a howling wilderness'), while both wrong answers are named cities (Nineveh, Babylon). The right answer stands out as a different kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke compares honey that God provides from a surprising place with Papa Dorin losing a chocolate chip in his mustache. Providing something and losing something are different actions, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card says Jeshurun is another name for Israel. That is a fact from outside the passage (for example, Deuteronomy 33:5 and Isaiah 44:2), and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The right answer ('By those who are not a people') reads like Bible wording and is a mirror-image phrase. The wrong answers are plain named groups ('priests of Egypt', 'kings of Canaan'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The story card is only a bare quote of 32:34. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice and no context for what 'these things' are.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the last word of a quoted line ('I wound and I ___'). That tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The story card is one flat sentence with no voice ('Then God lifts up His hand to heaven and makes a declaration.').

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card says 'The heavens rejoice, God's angels worship Him' as if it were happening. In 32:43 these are calls ('Rejoice, O heavens… let all God's angels worship Him'), not statements of what happens.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
